title: CRJA/25/2011 of MAHENDRA SINGH Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text: IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL

Criminal Jail Appeal No. 25 of 2011
Mahendra Singh
S/o Raghunath Singh
Ö..Ö Appellant

Versus
State of Uttarakhand
 ÖÖÖÖ. Respondent
Mr. A.M. Saklani, Amicus Curiae/ Advocate, present for the appellant
Mr. Aasif Ali, Brief Holder, present for the State.
Honʹble Prafulla C. Pant, J.
This appeal, received through Superintendent
of Sub-Jail Haldwani, is directed against the
judgment and order dated 10.05.2011, passed by
Additional Sessions Judge/Fast Track Court,
Kashipur, District Udham Singh Nagar, in Sessions
Trial No. 167 of 2008 whereby said court has
convicted accused/ appellant Mahendra Singh son of
Raghunath Singh under section 376 IPC and
sentenced him to rigorous imprisonment for a period
of eight years and directed to pay fine of ` 10,000/-.
The trial court has further directed that in case of
default in payment of fine the convict shall undergo
further imprisonment for a period of two months.

2
2. Heard learned Amicus Curiae for the appellant,
learned counsel for the State and perused the lower
court record.
3. Prosecution story, in brief, is that on 29.04.2008
at about 9:00 p.m., Kajal (victim) aged six years,
daughter of P.W.1 Lal Singh went to see of her friend
Neelam in Jeet Colony, Maheshpura, and when she
did not return to her home for quite sometime her
father (Lal Singh) went in search of his daughter.
After sometime he saw his little daughter was crying
by the side of playing ground and her trousers were
blood stained. She was bleeding from her private
parts. She was unable to disclose anything. On this
P.W.1 Lal Singh gave first information report (Ex.
A1) at police station Kashipur in the intervening
night of 29.04.2008/30.04.2008 at about 00:30 hours
against unknown person on the basis of which crime
no. 213 of 2008 was registered at police station
Kashipur relating to offence punishable under
section 376 IPC. P.W.6 Sub Inspector K.R. Sharma
investigated the crime. The victim was taken to L.D.
Bhatt Government Hospital, Kashipur, where she
was medically examined by P.W.7 Dr. Anjali Gupta
on 30.04.2008 who prepared injury report (Ex. A10).

3
In said report the medical officer (Dr. Anjali Gupta)
observed that she found oozing blood from vagina.
She further found that labiamijora and labiaminora
were inflamed. Hymen was found ruptured with
abrasions and cut on inlet of vagina. Tear found
extended up to anus area around rectum inflamed
and slight oozing of blood present. The victim was
thereafter sent for radiological examination and
P.W.4 Dr. T.K. Pant (Radiologist) after radiological
examination gave his report (Ex. A3) and opined that
the victim was aged between 4 to 6 years. It appears
that during investigation the accused Mahendra
Singh who was elder uncle (TAU) of the victim was
arrested and medically examined by P.W.1 Dr.
Madan Mohan of L.D.B. Government Hospital,
Kashipur on 01.05.2008. Said medical officer (Dr.
Madan Mohan) after medical examination of accused
Mahendra Singh found that there were mild
abrasions over peripheral margins of glans and
frenum beneath urethral opening. After
interrogating the witnesses and inspecting the spot,
the Investigating Officer submitted charge sheet (Ex.
A9) against accused Mahendra Singh for his trial in
respect of offence punishable under section 376 IPC.

4
4. Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Kashipur,
on receipt of the charge sheet, after giving necessary
copies to the accused as required under section 207
Cr.P.C., appears to have committed the case to the
court of Sessions for trial. On 26.07.2008 learned
Additional Sessions Judge, Kashipur, after hearing
the parties framed charge of offence punishable
under section 376 IPC against accused Mahendra
Singh who pleaded not guilty and claimed to be
tried on which prosecution got examined P.W.1 Lal
Singh (informant), P.W.2 Kajal (victim), P.W.3 Dr.
Madan Mohan (who medically examined the
accused), P.W.4 Dr. T.K. Pant (Radiologist), P.W.5
Head Constable Nanda Ballabh Tiwari (who
prepared check report), P.W.6 S.I. K. R. Sharma (who
investigated the crime), P.W.7 Dr. Anjali Gupta (who
medically examined the girl), P.W.8 Prem Singh
(declared hostile) and P.W.9 Longshree (declared
hostile).
5. Oral and documentary evidence was put to the
accused under section 313 Cr.P.C. in reply to which
he pleaded that evidence adduced against him was
false. No evidence in defence was adduced. The trial
court after hearing the parties found that prosecution

5
has successfully proved charge of offence punishable
under section 376 IPC against accused Mahendra
Singh and convicted him accordingly. After hearing
on sentence the convict was sentenced to rigorous
imprisonment for a period of eight years and
directed to pay fine of ` 10,000/-. Aggrieved by said
judgment and order dated 10.05.2011 passed by
Additional Sessions Judge/Fast Track Court,
Kashipur, in Sessions Trial No. 167 of 2008 this
appeal is got sent by the convict from Sub-Jail
Haldwani.
6. Before further discussion this Court thinks it
just and proper to mention the observations made by
P.W.7 Dr. Anjali Gupta on 30.04.2008 in her report
Ex. A10. Observations made by said medical officer
are reproduced below:-
Vaginal examination:- on inspection- Areas around
vagina, rectum are inflamed and very tender. Oozing of
blood present. Labia majora and Labia minora inflamed.
Hymen ruptured and abrasions present on the inlet
of vagina.
Tear extensive occurred in vaginal inlet and bleeding
(slight) present.

6
Abrasions and tear is very much tender, and b/c of
tenderness p/v examination is not possible.
Tear extended upto area of anus. Rectum inflamed
and light oozing of blood present.
7. Now it is necessary to mention the findings of
radiologist Dr. T.K. Pant (P.W.4) regarding age of the
victim. From the statement of the Radiologist read
with his report (Ex. A3) it is clear that after perusal of
x-ray of right elbow, right knee AP, right wrist of the
victim it was found that she was aged between 4-6
years.
8. Now it is also relevant to mention the findings
of P.W.3 Dr. Madan Mohan of L.D.Bhatt
Government Hospital, Kashipur, who medically
examined the private parts of accused Mahendra
Singh. From the injury/medical report prepared by
said medical officer (P.W.3) which is Ex. A2 on the
record it appears that though there was no blood
stain visible over glans and shaft of penis but there
were mild abrasions over peripheral margins of
glans and frenum beneath the uretheral opening.

7
9. Learned Amicus Curiae on behalf of the
appellant submitted that all the witnesses of fact
have turned hostile as such the trial court has erred
in law in convicting the accused under section 376
IPC.
10. I have carefully gone through the statements of
the witnesses. P.W.1 Lal Singh (informant) has
corroborated the prosecution story that on 24.02.2008
his daughter Kajal had gone to see of her friend
Neelam and when she did not return for sometime
he went in search of her. This witness further told
that he found his daughter behind his house and she
was crying. The witness further told that the trouser
of the girl was blood stained and she was bleeding
from her private parts. P.W.1 Lal Singh further
proved first information report lodged by him. He
was declared hostile on the ground that his little
daughter did not name accused Mahendra Singh to
him. Merely for this part of the statement made by
this witness of corroborating prosecution story
cannot be disbelieved. It is relevant to mention here
that in the FIR also this witness has also named any
accused.

8
11. P.W.2 Kajal (child victim) is the star witness of
the case. No doubt in her examination in chief
initially she has stated that her elder uncle
(Mahendra Singh) did not meet her on the day of the
incident but when she was cross-examined by the
public prosecutor she corroborated the fact that
during investigation she disclosed that her elder
uncle Mahendra Singh committed rape on her. Why
this witness has turned hostile is not difficult to be
answered. She is close relative of the accused, and it
cannot be ruled out that by the time she was
examined by the court she was got influenced by her
family members. Had there been no medical
evidence on record relating to private parts of the
victim and the accused it could have been said that
from the ocular testimony of the quality as above,
charge is not proved beyond reasonable doubt but in
view of the medical evidence on record of the victim,
and that of the accused read with ocular testimony of
P.W.1 Lal Singh and P.W.2 Kajal, this Court is in full
agreement with the trial court that prosecution has
successfully proved charge of offence punishable
under section 376 IPC against accused Mahendra
Singh.

9
12. Learned Amicus Curiae pleaded that the
sentence awarded by the trial court may be reduced
to the period already undergone. However,
considering the nature of the offence and age of the
victim, this Court is not inclined to interfere with the
sentence awarded by the trial court. (The State has
filed no appeal for enhancement of the sentence).
13. For the reasons as discussed above, this appeal
is liable to be dismissed. Accordingly, the appeal is
dismissed. Let a copy of this judgment be sent to the
Superintendent of jail concerned where appellant
Mahendra Singh (S/o Raghunath) is serving out the
sentence. Lower court record be sent back.
 (Prafulla C. Pant, J.)
Parul 24.05.2013
